title: central-policy-index-and-core-processes-2025
author: Asha Patel
body:
Purpose

This page is the single, consolidated index and reference for company-wide policies that affect every Redwoood Inference employee and system owner: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor lifecycle, travel policy, and the canonical internal templates. It defines owners, thresholds, SLOs, and step-by-step processes for common transactions. Treat this as the operational surface — individual, specialized policies (security, legal, team-level SOPs) are linked from the Related Pages column.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors working with Redwood Inference systems or data.
- Covers corporate systems (Okta, G Suite, Slack), cloud accounts (AWS/GCP projects), provisioning for Dedicated/Private deployments, and third-party services.
- Excludes team-specific dev playbooks; those live under team wiki pages and must reference this canonical policy.

Owners and Roles

1) Policy steward: Finance & Legal (owner_team) — responsible for policy maintenance, audit coordination, and procurement thresholds.
2) Access owner: IT & Security (operational lead) — manages Okta groups, SSO, and approval automation.
3) Data steward: Product Data Governance — classifies datasets and approves exception requests.
4) Vendor owner: Procurement & Vendor Ops — runs vendor onboarding and contract lifecycle.
5) Travel & Expenses owner: Finance Operations — manages Concur (or approved expense tool) config and audit.

Access & Permissions (Identity lifecycle)

Principles:
- Least privilege by default; roles and groups required for access must be pre-approved.
- All changes to privileged groups (admin, billing, infra) require 2-step approval: requestor manager + system owner.
- Access reviews: quarterly for admin & infra groups, annual for general productivity groups.

Tools and service names:
- Identity provider: Okta (SSO + SCIM for provisioning).
- Ticketing: JIRA (project: IT-ACCESS).
- Secrets: HashiCorp Vault (access controlled via Okta groups).

Standard request workflow:
1. Submit JIRA ticket (IT-ACCESS) with justification, manager approval, and expiry date.
2. IT reviews, verifies least-privilege assignment, and applies SCIM change.
3. If the change affects billing or infra scopes, Security must sign off within 48 hours.
4. System records updated; ticket closed with audit tag.

Change Management (configuration and infra changes)

SLOs and thresholds:
- Emergency changes: must be coordinated via Incident Manager; post-change RCA within 72 hours.
- Standard changes < $50k or without cross-regional impact: change advisory (email + JIRA RFC), 48h review.
- Large changes (>= $50k, cross-region, or affecting SLA): RFC + CAB approval; scheduled maintenance windows.

RFC process (high level):
1. Author prepares RFC in Confluence and links to JIRA change request (CHG-XXXX).
2. Technical reviewers and affected service owners review within 5 business days.
3. CAB (monthly or ad-hoc) approves or requests revisions.
4. Implement during agreed maintenance window with rollback steps documented.
5. Post-implementation verification and runbook updates.

Data Management (classification, handling, retention)

Classification levels:
- Public: no restrictions.
- Internal: default for product docs, non-sensitive logs.
- Confidential: PII-lite, customer usage metrics.
- Restricted: PII, customer data under contract, regulated data.

Handling rules:
- Restricted data must be stored in customer-project-scoped cloud resources with encryption at rest and restricted KMS access.
- No restricted data on personal devices or unapproved SaaS.
- Data access requests require Data Steward sign-off and a documented business justification.

Retention and deletion:
- Default retention for Internal/Confidential: 3 years.
- Restricted: retention per contract or legal hold; Data Steward coordinates deletions.

Procurement & Expenses

Thresholds and roles:
- Purchases <= $5,000: team lead approval in procurement tool.
- Purchases > $5,000 and <= $50,000: manager + Finance Ops approval.
- Purchases > $50,000: Procurement & Legal review and Exec sponsor.
- Subscription renewals auto-review at 60 days before renewal.

Process (step-by-step):
1. Create requisition in Procurement tool with business justification and cost center.
2. Obtain required approvals depending on threshold.
3. Procurement issues PO or vendor contract; Finance records ledger entry.
4. For capital expenses, route through Capital Approval workflow (FIN-CAPEX).

Expense policy highlights:
- Travel booked via Concur (or approved tool).
- Per diem: domestic $75/day, international $120/day unless actuals with receipts claimed.
- Hotel class: standard corporate (mid-market) unless Exec approval.
- Policy requires submission within 30 days of travel.

Vendor Management and Onboarding

Minimum requirements for onboarding third-party vendors:
- Completed vendor intake form in Procurement portal.
- Security questionnaire (SIG-lite or vendor-specific) completed and reviewed by Security.
- Contract with data processing addendum (DPA) when the vendor will process customer data.
- Risk tiering: Low, Medium, High — determines review cadence and required controls.

Lifecycle steps:
1. Intake & risk assessment.
2. Security review & remediation plan if needed.
3. Legal contract negotiation and signature.
4. Provision accounts and restrict access to necessary scopes.
5. Quarterly/annual reassessment based on tier.

Travel and Remote Work Travel Policy

Principles:
- Prioritize safety, cost-effectiveness, and compliance.
- All travel requires pre-approval; international travel requires manager + travel admin approval.

Booking & approvals:
1. Request in Concur with estimated costs and justification.
2. Manager approves; Finance Ops reviews for policy compliance.
3. For travel with customer sites, Sales Ops must confirm appointment.

Expense reimbursement:
- Itemized receipts required for all claims > $25.
- Monthly card reconciliations by cardholder; missed reconciliations escalate to manager.

Internal Templates and Standard Forms

Canonical templates (use by reference):
- Purchase Requisition Template (Procurement portal)
- Vendor Intake Form (Procurement)
- Access Request Form (IT-ACCESS JIRA template)
- RFC Template (Confluence/RFC template)
- Data Access Request (DAR) template
- Travel Request template (Concur link)

Each template includes required fields, approver chain, and audit checkpoints. Teams must not create ad-hoc forms that bypass these templates; request template changes by filing a doc-change PR with the Policy Steward.

Audits, Exceptions and Escalations

- Quarterly internal audits: access reviews, procurement sample checks, and vendor control validation.
- Exceptions: documented in Confluence with expiration and compensating controls; must be approved by Policy Steward + Owner.
- Escalation contacts: security@redwood.com (security issues), procurement@redwood.com (vendor/procurement), finance-ops@redwood.com (expenses).

Change log and maintenance

- Major policy revisions are versioned with date and rationale.
- This page maintained by Finance & Legal; technical process sections co-maintained with IT & Security.
- To propose a change: fork the policy in Confluence, add reviewer comments, and submit to Policy Steward for scheduling in the next review cycle.

Quick reference table (who to contact)

| Topic | Primary contact | Escalation | Tool/Project |
|------|----------------|-----------|--------------|
| Access & Permissions | IT & Security (it-access@redwood.com) | Security | JIRA (IT-ACCESS) |
| Change Management | Eng Ops | CTO Office | Confluence RFC / CHG-XXXX |
| Data Management | Product Data Governance | Legal | Data Catalog / DAR |
| Procurement | Procurement & Vendor Ops | Finance VP | Procurement Portal / PO |
| Travel & Expenses | Finance Ops | HR | Concur |

Appendices

A. Quick templates index: links to the template library and sample RFC.
B. Audit schedule and sample checklist.
C. Frequently asked questions and examples of acceptable justifications for access and procurement.

For questions or to request exceptions, contact the Policy Steward (policy-steward@redwood.com).

Last updated: 2025-11-02 (major revision: clarified procurement thresholds, added RFC cadence, updated travel per diem).
